page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the n2 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The system is configured with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the instance is tailored for memory capacity rather than raw computational speed. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance, along with Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, fall into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth tests for large blocks show uncached read speeds of 26.28 GB/sec and write speeds of 22.5 GB/sec, while Passmark memory scores reach an average rating. Single-threaded gzip compression performs at an average level of 23.92 GB/sec, whereas multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is poor, landing in the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highmem-4 offers high memory density relative to its processing resources, making it a viable option for workloads that require significant memory footprints without demanding high-performance compute. The instance is suited for memory-intensive applications such as caching layers, small database deployments, and lightweight data processing tasks where memory capacity is the primary constraint.
